# Reproducibility and known limits

| Gate | Asks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `verify_reproduction.R` | did the build reproduce the paper's exhibits? | **16 / 16** |
| `verify_manuscript_numbers.R` | does the rebuilt ledger agree with the paper? | digest match + **69 / 69** |
| `verify_semantics.R` | registers, exact inputs, claims, chart direction, the defect | **21 / 21** |
| `verify_governance.R` | does the receipt chain close? | **30 / 30** |

| `oracles/run_oracles.R` | do published, exhaustive, and boundary oracles agree? | **13 / 13** |

## The archival defect

`reference-code/R/core/ordinal-h.R` ships with a known defect: its transport
helper advances on a 1e-12 mass tolerance and can drop a valid tiny **positive**
mass. The corrected kernel lives in the separate `bayesmokken` package.

The helper compares each **current residual atom mass** with its tolerance,
before and after allocation. Depending on the pointer state, that residual can
be an original marginal category mass or a cross-CDF residual. Consequently the
exact vulnerable set is inclusive: (0 < \text{residual} \le 10^{-12}).

The claim is that no locked result is affected. **This package checks it by
direct execution.** `verification/archival/verify_archival_safety.R` rebuilds
all 168 population-truth configurations that called this helper: 36 Phase 14,
48 Phase 15 training, 36 Phase 15 validation, and 48 Phase 16.

Across those 168 configurations:

| | |
|---|---|
| residuals in `(0, 1e-12]` | **0** |
| smallest positive marginal category mass | **0.0155404871882598** |
| smallest positive cross-CDF gap | **1.93915947650503e-05** |
| maximum `abs(old H - corrected H)` | **0** |
| corrected-kernel mass-conservation failures | **0** |

Literal zero is safe: the old `<=` check advances it, and simultaneous exact
exhaustion advances both pointers. The Phase 16 table has eight **rows whose
scalar minimum is zero**; that is not a count of literal zero gaps. The full
certificate records all positive marginal masses, all positive cross-CDF gaps,
and direct old/corrected results instead of treating one scalar minimum as a
complete risk certificate.

The verifier also runs synthetic fixtures at `0.5e-12`, exactly `1e-12`, and
just above `1e-12`, plus an edge-mass case and literal-zero case. The first two
inclusive risk cases make old and corrected results diverge; the above-boundary
and literal-zero cases agree.

Per-replication point and bootstrap-draw calculations use the survival/`pmin`
kernel and bypass the defective helper. The helper was used for deterministic
population truths; the 168-row certificate therefore covers every locked
execution path to which this particular defect applies.

## The independent oracle lane

Two external checks:

**Transport, solved two ways.** A linear-programming solution against the
two-pointer implementation the method uses, across an exhaustive grid:
**3,362 cases across 32 strata, 0 failures**, maximum
|LP − corrected two-pointer| = 7.11e-15. A separate five-case boundary grid
covers literal zero, residuals below/at/above `1e-12`, and a tiny edge mass.

**Koopman et al. (2022), reproduced.** Both scales recomputed from
`data(SWMDK)` with `mokken`:

| Scale | Published | Recomputed |
|---|---|---|
| teacher | 0.62 | 0.6199 |
| classmate | 0.592 | 0.5923 |

And this article's own locked teacher value to |diff| = 5.76e-14.

::: {.callout-important}
An oracle failure is a finding about the **method**, not about the packaging.
Do not reconcile it against the locked artifact.
:::

## A gate that cannot fail is not a gate

| Control | Gate |
|---|---|
| corrupt a float | `verify_reproduction` |
| perturb one ledger value | `verify_manuscript_numbers` |
| **reverse the calibration-direction claim** | `verify_semantics` |
| plant an absolute path | `disclosure_scan` |
| add a file with no ledger verdict | `disclosure_scan` |
| drop the SWMDK object-digest record | `verify_governance` |
| **delete the archival-defect banner** | `verify_semantics` |
| change nothing | all five must pass |

The direction control matters here because this calibration **tightens** while
the companion paper's widens. A check that merely asserted "the calibration
changes the length" would pass on either, and would be worthless.

## Known limits

**Cross-platform raster identity.** Figure parity hashes a `pdftoppm` render at
150 dpi, so the hash depends on the Poppler build. Matching geometry with
differing pixels is more likely a renderer difference than a scientific one.

**This reproduces the analysis snapshot, not the production runs.** The Phase 16
confirmation and Phase 17 application ran on AWS and are documented, not
enabled.

**The application data is not ours to ship.** Every application number is
conditional on the `SWMDK` object in your `mokken` install. The lock makes a
mismatch loud rather than silent, but it cannot prevent one.

**The receipt chain is scoped** to the v4 receipts; see
[governance](08-governance.qmd).

**The manuscript-text checks live with the manuscript** — the needle half of
each concordance check, and the six-phrase claim-boundary audit, run where the
`.tex` is.

## Two traps worth knowing

`grep` silently skips Latin-1 TeX logs as binary — zero hits can mean "did not
read". Use `grep -a`.

`data.table::fread()` given a `.gz` path decompresses it in place, mutating the
frozen snapshot. The readers here open `gzfile()` connections.
